question.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, an angular width of the fringe is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo></math> on a screen placed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> away for particular wavelength of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>450</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>. The angular width of the fringe, when whole system is immersed in a medium of refractive index <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>α</mi></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Angular fringe width is given by θ=λD, where, D is the distance between the source and the screen and λ is the wavelength of the light.

We have, θ1θ2=λ1λ2

Then, θ2=0.35∘450 nm×450 nm75=0.25∘=14   ∵λ2=λ1μ

Thus, value of α=4.
